chapter: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
title: Taking George E. Lee's chair in Kansas City
summary: After Stone's band breaks up, Budd sits in George E. Lee's chair, gets the job, and notes he reached Chicago January 9, 1932.

bands.name: Jesse Stone and His Blue Serenaders

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: After I left Jesse STONE, see, the band finally broke up. I told you, and then Keg went to Minneapolis to join Eli Rice, and whatnot, right? And by this time I'm seeking a job.

So I told you we had met George E. Lee, and in Saint Joseph, Missouri, and they remembered me, and they dug the band, and everything, so one day I went by George E. Lee's rehearsal, and he wasn't there, so I just took my horn out and sat in his chair. So when he finally appeared I'm sitting in his chair playing. He say, "What, you came to take my job?" I said, "That's right." So he says, "Well then you've got it." 'Cause he played saxophone and sang.
So he just sang then, and let me play the saxophone, 'cause they liked the way I played. So now I'm with George E. Lee, and this is all like --
Now George E. Lee is where I like kind of come in with you, isn't it, Budd?
You came to Milwaukee then, didn't you? Didn't you come to Milwaukee with George E. Lee?
No. No, this was before. This was
Yeah, but I didn't hit Chicago until January the 9th, 1932.
1932. Oh, that's great, because I didn't really know that date, and I had my first meeting with you. And when was that, Budd?
I came to Chicago January the 9th, 1932, and now I'm in '29 with George E. Lee.
